abstract: Recent improvements in long-read sequencing accuracy, particularly the introduction of PacBio HiFi reads, have created new opportunities for more efficient sequence representations in genome assembly. In particular, variations of de Bruijn graphs (dBG), such as sparse dBG and minimizer-space dBG, provide efficient representations of sequences and have enabled genome assemblers to leverage the high accuracy of long-read data while maintaining low memory usage and fast analysis times. Locally consistent parsing (LCP) is another technique for compact sequence representation that partitions a string into nearly uniform, highly distinctive substrings in a consistent manner. In this work, we combine ideas from minimizer-space assembly and LCP to achieve a significant speedup in HiFi long-read assembly. Specifically, we define a locally consistent de Bruijn Graph (lcDBG), in which string partitions serve as the graph's building blocks. We introduce Gallifrey, a rapid PacBio HiFi assembler that outperforms the fastest existing tool, rust-mdbg, by >6x in runtime while requiring 2x less memory, assembling a human genome in under one minute on a standard laptop, while generating assemblies with comparable contiguity. Code for Gallifrey is freely available at https://github.com/BilkentCompGen/gallifrey.
